topic.title: Video Representation, Action Structure, and Skill Transfer
topic.overview: Understanding video requires connecting appearance with temporal structure, object interactions, and actions. This topic studies self-supervised representations, structured object tokens, motion models, and reusable skill descriptions. It asks how information from images, language, and observed dynamics can support recognition or transfer to new action compositions.
topic.whyItMatters: Dense video annotation is costly, so useful methods extract supervision from consistency or reuse sparse structured labels. Temporal reasoning must still distinguish actual motion and interaction from static scene cues. For action models, recognizing a familiar pattern and executing a new composition require different evidence.
topic.evolution: A 1993 gesture system combines spatial representations with dynamic time warping. Later work learns video dynamics and recurrent representations without dense labels. StructureViT in 2022 transfers image-level hand-object structure through frame-clip consistency; SkillNet in 2026 organizes mechanical and semantic skill attributes to guide compositional transfer in vision-language action models.
openQuestions: Which temporal objectives prevent models from solving video tasks through static shortcuts?
How can reusable skill representations support genuinely unfamiliar compositions of actions?
